report: User screenshot: pelican head appears missing in V3 rear chase view. Treat as avatar readability complaint and reproduce the exact straight/catch presentation branch.

scope.rationale: Camera/head animation presentation is on default core journey; preserve validated user media, exact branch and independent perceptual retest.

steps: Capture default straight ride and catch in current build
Check same head object during turn, jump, stun and replay on both engines
observed: Crop shows rear body and tiny helmet silhouette; head/beak identity unclear
Original head and beak geometry definitions remain present; actual occlusion/gaze cause needs branch test

Final current20 diagnosis: the authorized demo state has no yaw field. Default idle/menu pose synchronization had used that undefined yaw in native head IK before the first run, producing non-finite native head transforms. syncRidePose initializes a complete finite idle pose (yaw/lean/steer=0), and copies real adventure pose before native IK during play. Original head/neck/beak geometry and its .355 neck/28-degree gaze remain unchanged; the initial geometry hypothesis was rejected and reverted.

Current20 exact head object is finite and connected in both real browser engines at390×844,360×740,320×568,844×390 across natural straight/catch/turn/jump/pedestrian-stop/recovery/replay. Independent48-cell head matrix is hash-bound. Rear chase naturally hides the forward-facing beak in some frames; beak-animation and original screenshot capture revision are not claimed verified.

acceptanceCriteria: Head/neck/beak recognisable in default mobile straight/catch view
Preserve road, all lanes and forward hazard readability
No forced camera orbit or body yaw changes
Capture exact branch with natural touch on both engines and four sizes
